CITY OF ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
  COMMISSION
  THURSDAY, MAY 8, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Environmental Sustainability Commission will be held on Thursday, May 8,
2025 at 6:00 p.m. in Conference Room A, on the second floor of the Alhambra
City Hall, 111 S. First St., Alhambra, California, pursuant to the order of the
Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission Secretary.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Latoya Waters,
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability
  Commission Secretary

Notice No. N2M25-57
Posted: 5/5/2025
   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  May 8, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

 I.  ROLL CALL
  Xana Hermosillo, Scott Chan, Michael Scaduto, Katie Chan

II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 03-13-2025 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

 III.  GREEN STREET DEMONSTRATION PROJECT ON MAIN STREET UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Green Street Demonstration Project on Main Street.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

 IV.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

 V.  AIR QUALITY AND AIR FILTER STUDY UPDATE
  API Forward Movement will provide and update on the Air Quality and Air Filter Study

 VI.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  The Environmental Sustainability Commission will discuss action items for the next meeting.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

 VII.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit
  all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior to the
  meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5) minutes.

 VIII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

 IX.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, July 10, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

  1
  05/08/2025
 If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the
Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact Latoya Waters, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on March 13, 2025

The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
order at 6:09 p.m. on March 13, 2025.

I.  ROLL CALL
  Commission Members Present: Katie Chan, Scott Chan, Xana Hermosillo, Amy
  Wong

  Commission Member Absent: Lisa Massaro

  Staff Present: Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager; Katie Martel, Sustainability
  Analyst, serving as Commission Secretary for this meeting

  Members of the Public: Raudell Aluiso, Lahiru Kodituwakku

II.  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES
  The Commission reviewed and approved the minutes from the previous meeting
  on November 14, 2024, with some minor adjustments noted to be reflected in
  minutes.

  Commissioner S. Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from November
  14, 2024, as amended. Commissioner Wong seconded the motion. All
  Commissioners present voted in favor to approve the minutes. Motion passed.

III.  ELECTION OF OFFICERS
  The commission discussed the need for a new commission president due to a
  change in commission members. Commissioner K. Chan nominated herself for
  the role. No other commission members were nominated or self-nominated.

  Commissioner Hermosillo motioned to elect Commissioner K. Chan as the
  president of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Commissioner S.
  Chan seconded the motion. All Commissioners present voted in favor to approve
  the minutes. Motion passed.

  Commissioner K. Chan was elected as the new president of the Environmental
  Sustainability Commission. Commissioner Hermosillo will remain as the vice
  president.
 IV.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager, provided an update on the City’s
  Sustainability Plan, currently in the development process.

  Phase 1 involved early data collection and community engagement to understand
  priorities and concerns around sustainability. Now, Phase 2 is focused on more
  community engagement, including town hall meetings and online surveys to
  gather feedback on proposed strategies and actions. Partner agencies and
  organizations, such as ActiveSGV, South Coast Air Quality Management District
  and APIFM, were invited to host booths at the town halls to share information
  about programs, projects and financial incentives available for Alhambra
  residents and businesses. In addition, City staff hosted a booth at the Lunar New
  Year Festival and will be at the Eco Fair event in April, to talk with residents
  about the sustainability plan and promote the online survey.

  The next steps include additional data collection and extensive analysis to include
  in the draft plan which will be prepared by the fall. The Commission will have
  the opportunity to provide input and feedback on the draft plan. City Council
  adoption of the final plan is targeted for late 2025. The City Council has
  identified the sustainability plan as a key focus area in their strategic planning.
  .
V.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY DISCUSSION
  The commission discussed the need for more information on current
  sustainability projects and funding sources, including potential federal and state
  funding opportunities.

  There was a request for more advance notice and broader geographic distribution
  of the community engagement events.

  The commission expressed interest in receiving updates on specific sustainability
  initiatives, such as the stormwater capture project, at the next meeting.

  The commission also requested information on sustainability plans from
  neighboring cities to help inform their own plan development.

VI.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Raudell Aluiso from the Community Health Alliance presented concerns about
  secondhand smoke exposure in Alhambra, particularly in multi-unit housing. The
  organization recommended that the City consider adopting comprehensive
  smoke-free policies for multi-unit housing to protect public health and prevent
  fire risks. Examples were provided of other cities in the county that have
  implemented such policies.

VII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Commissioner Hermosillo shared that she participated in an air quality monitoring
  study conducted by USC and APIFM.

VIII. ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner K. Chan adjourned the meeting at 6:39 p.m.
